newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS -- BP Ohio plant closure part of global plan.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS -- BP Ohio plant closure part of global plan.

text.p: BP America's failure to secure a buyer for its refinery in Lima, Ohio comes as no surprise in an industry where thin margins have forced a slew of mergers, closures and consolidations in recent years, analyst said.
The company, the U.S. unit of British Petroleum Co plc, said on Friday that it received three bids for the plant, which was put up for sale earlier this year, but that all were unacceptable.

BP said it will stop operating the 161,000 barrels-per-day plant as an oil refinery in two years, but will keep the nearby chemicals plant open and will operate the site as a distribution terminal. Most of the 475 jobs at the plant will go unless an eleventh-hour savior steps in.
"It's in a localized niche area, so you're not going to attract too many buyers," said Ken Miller, senior principal of Purvin & Gertz Inc, a Houston-based oil consultancy.

"We kind of expected it," said one oil executive who didn't want to be named. "BP is doing the same thing they did with Marcus Hook," he added, referring to the Philadelphia-area refinery shut this February after BP sold it to Tosco Corp in December.
Tosco subsequently decided to reopen that plant next year. But unlike Marcus Hook, which is located on the populous East Coast, the Lima plant is in a small market with too much competition.

"In general terms there's plenty of capacity around, particularly on the Gulf Coast, to keep that region supplied with products," said Miller, noting U.S. refiners have been able to boost products output at a rate of one percent a year for the last several years just by improving efficiency at existing units.
Friday's announcement comes as part of BP's broader downstream strategy, which has evolved since the beginning of this year as new chief executive John Browne took the helm.

In January, BP said it would sell or close three-loss-making refineries, including the Lima plant, its Lavera, France operation and the Pernis section of the Nerefco refinery near Rotterdam in the Netherlands. The plans would result in a $1.1 billion charge for the group.
In February, BP announced a $5 billion link-up with Mobil of the two oil giants' downstream European assets, bringing together 8,900 service stations and saving between $400 and $500 million a year.

The refinery closures would bring BP's down to 11 worldwide and bring its refinging-to-marketing ratio more into line with other majors. But Browne has said that, even if all three ended up closed, they wouldn't make any material impact on worldwide overcapacity.
